sentences.text: Here is what the dead do.
They do not hunt.
They repeat.
They arrive around seven.
They lean on the shutter all day.
But when the sun goes down and the air turns cold, they stop.
Not drift off.
Stop.
They stand in the lot like statues until morning.
You do not know why.
You write it on the wall anyway.
So you work at night, and you live on the roof.
You cook on a camping stove, never indoors.
In a sealed building, a gas flame will kill you more quietly than they ever could.
On day four, the taps run dry.
You have eight pallets of bottled water, so drinking is easy.
The toilets are the problem.
One bucket, one bin bag, and a trip to aisle 13 for cat litter.
On day five, Rhea's van pulls into the staff lot.
It stops perfectly between the lines.
The engine runs until the tank is empty.
When you finally climb down, the driver's door is open and the seat is empty.
On the dashboard sits a child's drawing of a house.
Somebody has smashed the passenger window from the inside.
Every night at 9:00, you hear it.
Three knocks, a pause, three more.
It is not coming from the doors.
It is coming from the walk-in freezer.
On day nine, you are asleep on a pile of dog beds when the ceiling turns white.
Every light blazes and every freezer roars.
And from the speakers, the intercom wakes up.
Attention shoppers, says a voice.
The store is now closing.
It says your name.
Outside, 250 heads turn at once.
